branchSettings.title: Branch settings
branchSettings.subtitle: Choose the main branch and control how data and financial records are shared between branches.
branchSettings.main_branch_hint: The main branch is the primary reference for managing data and financial records across all branches.
branchSettings.share_customers_desc: Let all branches access customer data to avoid duplication and serve the same customer from any branch. When disabled, each branch keeps its own customers.
branchSettings.share_products_desc: Share products and services across all branches to unify prices and descriptions and avoid duplication. When disabled, each branch adds its own products. Stock availability per branch depends on warehouses, regardless of sharing.
branchSettings.share_suppliers_desc: Share the supplier list across branches to unify dealings and create purchase orders from one base. When disabled, each branch keeps its own suppliers.
branchSettings.share_cost_centers_desc: Link cost centers across branches to track expenses and revenue per center, enabling company-wide financial analysis. When disabled, each branch has its own cost centers.
branchSettings.account_branch_scoping_desc: Allocate each account at branch level to record financial transactions and follow accounting results separately. An account can be assigned to one branch, several, or all.
branchSettings.footer_note: Choose how data and financial records are shared between branches to unify or separate your operations. Existing records are shared once enabled.

purchaseForm.title: New purchase invoice
purchaseForm.search_supplier: Enter a name, phone or tax number
purchaseForm.search_product: Search by name, SKU or barcode…
purchaseForm.need_line: Add at least one line with a quantity and a price.
purchaseForm.items_hint: A line with an inventory-tracked product enters stock (account 1140). A non-tracked service product — shipping or clearance — is an expense on account 5150 and does not touch stock.
purchaseForm.s_discount_hint: Invoice- or line-level discount and rounding adjustment. Needs new columns on the purchase and its lines plus journal entries to review — next batch.
purchaseForm.s_shipping_hint: Invoice-level shipping fees. Today they are entered as a descriptive line and go to expenses — which is a correct treatment.
purchaseForm.s_attachments_hint: Upload the supplier's invoice image and keep it with the document. Needs file storage, not built yet.
purchaseForm.product_required: Every line needs a product. For shipping or clearance create a non-inventory service product — it still posts to expenses.
purchaseForm.head_amounts_hint: Discount and shipping go into the cost of the goods themselves: the discount lowers the moving average, and inbound freight is capitalised onto it (IAS 2). The adjustment is a rounding difference on account 5170 that touches neither inventory nor tax.
purchaseForm.paid_hint: A posted payment voucher is issued when the bill is posted: debit 2110 payables / credit cash or bank. A partial amount leaves the rest as a real debt to the supplier.
purchaseForm.paid_cash_hint: A cash bill is settled in full on posting via an automatic voucher. For a partial payment choose credit.
purchaseForm.receipt_hint: Two informational fields separating the bill date from the date the goods arrived. Stock still enters on posting either way.

salesSettings.title: Sales settings
salesSettings.subtitle: Defaults used across invoices and quotes
salesSettings.hub_subtitle: Configure invoices, payments, quotes, and sales orders.
salesSettings.c_invoices_d: Control invoice templates and how they appear in the system.
salesSettings.c_statuses_d: Customize invoice statuses and apply them across orders and sales reports.
salesSettings.c_einvoice_d: Set up and link e-invoices and receipts with the tax authority.
salesSettings.c_designs_d: Design and customize print/preview templates for sales documents.
salesSettings.c_fields_d: Control custom invoice fields across the available field types.
salesSettings.c_pricelists_d: Create and manage price lists, applied by customer or transaction type.
salesSettings.c_sources_d: Create custom order sources to classify and track sales and POS documents.
salesSettings.c_shipping_d: Define shipping methods, rates, delivery and cash-on-delivery settings.
salesSettings.c_quotes_d: Configure how quotes are created, managed, and converted to invoices.
salesSettings.c_orders_d: Control how sales orders are issued, managed, and converted to invoices.
salesSettings.default_terms_hint: Terms printed on the invoice are set in
salesSettings.require_return_source_on: Required — no return without a source
salesSettings.require_return_source_hint: A business policy, not an accounting rule: retail wants “no refund without a receipt”, while services issue standalone credit notes for negotiated settlements. Either way, a linked return can never exceed its invoice’s quantity or price — that limit cannot be switched off.
salesSettings.return_window_days_hint: Measured from the invoice date. “0” means no limit — the default. A business policy, not an accounting rule: retail publishes a fixed window, while contracting and long-term agreements have none. It does not apply to a return without a source document, which has no reference date.

warehouses.title: Warehouses
warehouses.subtitle: Warehouses hold product quantities per location; cost valuation stays unified company-wide.
warehouses.name: Name
warehouses.branch_hint: Link to a branch to make it that branch default sales warehouse; leave empty for a central warehouse.
warehouses.is_default_hint: Receives movements with no explicit warehouse. Only one per company.
warehouses.is_active_hint: Inactive warehouses are not selectable for new movements.

inventorySettings.title: Inventory and product settings
inventorySettings.subtitle: Control product behaviour, tracking mechanisms, stocktaking and warehouse permits.
inventorySettings.detailed_tracking: Track products by serial number, batch number or expiry date
inventorySettings.detailed_tracking_hint: Tracks every unit or batch individually with its own cost and expiry, issuing by earliest expiry first. Not built yet — it requires a per-batch cost layer that changes how the cost of goods sold is computed.
inventorySettings.policy_block_all: Stop operations when stock runs out, for all products
inventorySettings.policy_block_all_hint: Prevents selling or using any product when no quantity is in stock. This applies to products tracked by quantity, serial number, batch number or expiry date.
inventorySettings.policy_allow_quantity: Allow only for products tracked by quantity
inventorySettings.policy_allow_quantity_hint: Negative stock is allowed only for products tracked by quantity, not for those tracked by serial number, batch number or expiry date.
inventorySettings.negative_stock_hint: Choose how the system handles negative stock. The policy applies to sales invoices, point of sale and purchase returns.
inventorySettings.allow_warning: Allowing negative stock does double damage: the inventory account (1140) ends up with a credit balance although it is an asset, and the moving average is corrupted by every later purchase, so the cost of goods sold comes out wrong. Use the inventory diagnostic report to see the affected items.
inventorySettings.show_stock_quantities: Show total and available warehouse quantity for products
inventorySettings.show_stock_quantities_hint: When off, the quantity is hidden from the product list and the product card. This option affects no balance and no journal entry — display only.
inventorySettings.total_in_stock_hint: Determines how quantity is checked on sale or issue: total stock, or what is available after deducting reserved quantities. Not built yet — there is no concept of a reserved quantity in the system today, so total and available are one number.
inventorySettings.c_products_d: Control product behaviour, tracking mechanisms, stocktaking and warehouse permits.
inventorySettings.c_categories_d: Create multi-level categories to group items and make filtering in lists and reports easier.
inventorySettings.c_brands_d: Create any number of brands to classify items, simplify managing them and link them to reports.
inventorySettings.c_units_d: Define base units and conversion ratios so you can buy and sell products in different units.
inventorySettings.c_employee_warehouses_d: Assign default warehouses to employees to track their permissions, stock movements and permits.
inventorySettings.c_barcode_d: Set barcode preferences and formats for accurate scanning and weight-based pricing.
inventorySettings.c_fields_d: Add custom fields to capture extra data and show it on product pages, lists and reports.
inventorySettings.unit_base_hint: The stock unit — every quantity in the ledger is counted in it.
inventorySettings.unit_factor_hint: The factor is how many “{base}” make one unit. It starts at 2 and takes no fractions: a unit smaller than the base is handled by making the smaller one the base. Changing a factor later never touches a posted document — the line copies its factor when it is created.
inventorySettings.restock_sales_returns_hint: A business policy, not an accounting rule: retail puts sound goods back on the shelf, while restaurants and food shops never restock a return. Either way, the amount refunded to the customer is unchanged.
inventorySettings.restock_off_note: When off: returned goods do not enter stock and the moving average is untouched; their cost is posted to “5180 Inventory Adjustments” instead of “1140 Inventory”. You can override this per return on its creation screen.

purchaseSettings.title: Purchase settings
purchaseSettings.subtitle: Defaults applied to purchase documents and bills. No accounting effect on their own.
purchaseSettings.default_tax_rate_hint: Applied to any line without an explicit rate.
purchaseSettings.default_payment_type_hint: Used when generating a bill from a purchase order without one.
purchaseSettings.default_tax_inclusive_hint: Inclusive: the price already contains tax, which is extracted from it.
purchaseSettings.require_return_source_on: Required — no return without a source
purchaseSettings.require_return_source_hint: Independent of the sales switch: you may require a receipt to refund a customer yet not require an invoice to return goods to a supplier. Either way, a linked return can never exceed its source quantity or price.
purchaseSettings.return_window_days_hint: Measured from the bill date. “0” means no limit — the default. Independent of the sales window: you may set a window for your customers yet be bound by none with your suppliers.

stockPermits.title: Stock permits
stockPermits.draft_hint: Draft: no quantity moved and no entry posted yet.
stockPermits.entry_posted: Posted: quantity moved and the matching entry was created in the same operation.
stockPermits.no_entry_internal: Transfer within the same branch — quantity moved between warehouses with no entry, so nothing changed in the general ledger.

stocktaking.title: Stocktaking
stocktaking.open_hint: Opening snapshots the warehouse balances at that moment — so the count sheet stays evidence of what was, not of what changed after.
stocktaking.draft_hint: Counting: no quantity moved and no entry posted yet. An empty field means "not counted" and is skipped; zero means "counted, none found" and writes the balance off.
stocktaking.entry_posted: Posted: quantities corrected and the difference entry created in the same operation.
stocktaking.no_difference: Posted with no difference — the count matched exactly, so no entry.
